procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism: Register the factory through the Factory Registration service, which requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority: Require the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately in its own right.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade: Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade: Fill in the application form and upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade: The applicant pays the fee online; the fee ranges from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on the invoice value.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade: Submit the application and receive approval, or a return with comments to correct.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade: Print the approved certificate.
The competent authority: Issue the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation; it is valid for twelve months from the date of issue and for only one import.

The exporter: Ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
The exporter: Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the year of the date of issue of the certificate.
The Indian importer: Claim the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed, for at least five years from filing.

caveats.note: The agreement does not define '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%'; Mansha interprets it as 'and' (both tests must pass).
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Article 3.5.1 does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
Cumulation is bilateral only; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
The agreement says box 8 for the certificate, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
